title: Candidate quantization profile evaluation and scorer bridge for accuracy validation
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: As we expand support for FP8 and INT8 model variants in runtime-1.20, we need a repeatable evaluation framework that links quantization profiles and calibration outputs to concrete quality metrics. This ticket creates a lightweight 'scorer bridge' that standardizes metric calculation (perplexity, MMLU-style accuracy, Rouge/BLEU, task-specific scorers like EM/F1 for QA) across calibration jobs and produces artifacts for CI gating and the console QA dashboard.

Goals:
- Define canonical scoring interfaces and thresholds for FP8 and INT8 candidate profiles.
- Implement a reusable scorer module used by calibration jobs and offline evals.
- Add automated checks that fail a quantization rollout candidate if regressions exceed defined tolerances.
- Produce artifacts (JSON reports, summary CSVs) and push to S3 and evaluation dashboard for longitudinal tracking.

Scope exclusions: This ticket does not alter kernel selection or runtime serving paths; it focuses on evaluation, reporting, and CI integration. Model retraining or GPTQ algorithm changes are out-of-scope and will be tracked separately.
acceptance_criteria: Scorer module implemented and published as a pip package internal to repo (redwood-quant-scorer).
Perplexity, MMLU-style micro/macro accuracy, Rouge-1/2/L, BLEU-4, and task-specific scorers (EM/F1 for QA, ROUGE for summarization, ranking metrics for rerankers) are available and documented.
Calibration jobs produce standardized report JSON (schema v1) including per-batch stats, token-level distributions, and metric deltas vs float32 baseline.
CI gating rule added: any candidate profile with >1.5% absolute drop on critical MMLU subset or >5% relative increase in perplexity for chat models will fail the pipeline.
Evaluation artifacts are wired to the QA dashboard (grafana/gcp-eval) and S3 at s3://redwood-evals/quant/ENG-6241/.
Runbook added to Confluence with instructions to reproduce calibration and scoring locally and troubleshoot false positives in CI.
Unit tests and example evals (small MMLU sample + toy summarization set) exist and run in CI under the quant-eval job.
Performance: scorer module adds <10% walltime to existing calibration pipeline for a 1B-parameter model when run on the standard eval node.
